Item: What carries the front edge when the desk is open?
Prompt / specification: User lean, typing, and accidental edge loading create leverage far from the wall. Options: Rated supports tied through the cabinet or ledger into verified structure | Folding legs that lock on the floor | A piano hinge alone

Item: How will cables move as the desk closes?
Prompt / specification: Power bricks, plugs, and cable loops can jam the hinge or be crushed behind the panel. Options: Model a strain-relieved flexible loop through the complete arc | Disconnect and store devices before closing | Leave slack behind the hinge

Item: How will the closed desk stay secured?
Prompt / specification: A panel can fall open if a magnet, latch, or support is undersized or misaligned. Options: Use positive latches rated and positioned for the finished panel | Use two tested cabinet catches plus a secondary restraint | Depend on hinge friction

Prompt / specification: A required fastener lands outside known structure, spins, or relies on an unidentified cavity anchor.

Prompt / specification: A bracket binds, snaps, overtravels, or loses level between partly open and fully open positions.
Project value / evidence: Stop cycling, reproduce the full section in a mockup, and correct pivot and mounting geometry using the actual hardware.

Prompt / specification: A cable scuffs, tightens, folds sharply, or enters the hinge, support, or latch during movement.
Project value / evidence: Disconnect power, relocate strain relief and clips, then complete repeated cycles with the largest real connector.

Prompt / specification: The panel drifts open, bounces away from bumpers, or releases when the wall or case is touched.
Project value / evidence: Keep the area clear and install a tested positive latch and secondary restraint for the finished panel mass.

Prompt / specification: The folding desk has two stable, intentional states and a verified transition that never asks cables, fingers, latches, or wall finish to carry work load.
The open work surface returns to the released level after repeated full open-and-close cycles.
